title: Chen Nian Appears
next_chapter_hook: Chen Nian points toward the Void—those eyes invisible to mortal sight are watching. They are more terrifying than the Eyes of Heavenly Dao, for they are the Chess Player who wove this ten-thousand-year chess game.

text.content: Before the morning fog had dispersed, the turtle shell mark in Chen Ji's hand still glowed with a dim light. He read the secret letter three times over, each character seeming to carve itself into his bones. Suburban ruined temple, unsigned, only one sentence: 'The old friend shall return.' The handwriting was unfamiliar, yet at the final stroke's conclusion, there was a faint arc he knew all too well—the starting habit he had deliberately corrected when teaching his little sister to write.

dialogue.content: The voice of the Soul Fragment Guardian drifted from the first page with a playful tone: 'Suburban ruined temple, three sides exposed to wind, no shelter—this place is interestingly chosen. I wonder what kind of person dares summon you, Chen Ji, to such a location?'

text.content: Chen Ji remained silent. His gaze fixed on that arc, his fingertips trembling slightly. Ten years had passed, and he had almost believed that name existed only in memory. Chen Nian—his sister, the one taken by the Holy Sect. He orchestrated the world, his calculations flawless, yet this matter alone was the deepest obsession in his heart, and the only blind spot the Tianji Record could not reach.

choice.prompt: Facing this letter that may conceal deadly intent, how should Chen Ji respond?

choices.description: Regardless of whether it is a trap, he must confirm it himself. This may be the only clue about his sister.
choices.visible_reward: Possibility of Reunion with His Sister
choices.risk_hint: If There is an Ambush, He Will Be Isolated and Defenseless

text.content: Chen Ji tucked the secret letter into his sleeve, his expression already restored to calm as he rose. He informed no one, not even bringing the short sword that never left his side. Mr. Mo's voice sounded behind him: 'Be careful. I am not eager to find a replacement so soon.'

The suburban ruined temple was more decrepit than he had imagined. Wild grass ran rampant among the broken walls, a mutilated stone statue half-buried in dust, the Buddha's head long vanished. The moment Chen Ji stepped through the temple gate, the morning wind abruptly ceased, and even the birdsong disappeared.

choices.description: Send trusted subordinates to set an ambush nearby while he scouts ahead. If anything unusual occurs, retreat immediately.
choices.risk_hint: If Discovered, May Alert the Prey

text.content: Chen Ji did not depart immediately. Summoning two trusted subordinates from the shadows, he quietly gave them instructions. Half an hour later, within a three-li radius of the ruined temple, three hidden sentry points had been discreetly established. Only then did he walk alone into the morning fog, his steps neither hasty nor slow.

choices.description: This letter arrives too conveniently—first use the Tianji Record to divine before proceeding.
choices.visible_reward: Gain Foresight of the Meeting's Outcome
choices.risk_hint: Heavenly Fate is precious, and the Tianji Record is blind to her

text.content: He closed his eyes, and the fragment of the Tianji Record unfolded slowly in his consciousness. Yet what made his heart sink was that whenever the vision touched upon the characters 'Chen Nian,' it was like a stone dropped into a deep pool—after the ripples spread, only chaos remained. He spent five Heavenly Fate Points, only to receive a vague outline: within the ruined temple, someone waits.

The temple was dim, only a shaft of light leaking through a hole in the roof, illuminating the dusty ground. At the edge of that shaft stood a figure. Her features were invisible against the light, but her form—slender yet upright—was no longer that little girl who used to hide behind him and tug at his clothes begging for candy.

dialogue.content:
"Brother."

The voice was soft, as if afraid to disturb anything. Yet this single word froze Chen Ji in place. He had witnessed countless grand scenes, orchestrated earth-shaking chess games, but now his throat felt blocked, unable to speak for a long moment.

text.content: As the light shifted, her features finally came into view. Chen Nian had grown half a head taller over the past decade, all her childhood innocence gone, replaced by an air of heroism and... an indescribable resilience. A faint scar marked her left brow, its origin unknown. The girl who once cried at the slightest provocation now stood resolute, eyes reddened yet holding back tears.

dialogue.content: "I know what you're thinking." Chen Nian stepped forward, voice trembling with suppressed emotion. "'Grown up,' right? I think so too. Ten years, brother. Ten whole years." Her fingers clenched her sleeves, knuckles white. "When those people took me away back then, I waited every day, wondering when you would come to rescue me. Eventually, I stopped waiting. I decided... I wanted to become strong, strong enough to find you myself."

text.content: Chen Ji finally moved, walking slowly as if stepping on knife points. He wanted to say so much—inquire about her wellbeing, ask if she suffered, pour out a decade of guilt. Yet in the end, he simply raised his hand and gently placed it on her head, just like when they were children.

dialogue.content:
"You've grown tall." His voice was hoarse, carrying a tremor he hadn't noticed himself. "Taller than me."

Chen Nian finally couldn't hold back any longer. Tears spilled out even as she smiled, playfully hitting his chest: "Fool, I haven't finished talking!" That punch carried no force at all, yet it shattered some hard barrier deep within Chen Ji's heart.

choice.prompt: After their reunion, how should Chen Ji bring up the truth?

choices.description: "All these years... how did you manage?" Let her tell her story first, then ask for crucial information.

text.content: Chen Ji guided her to sit on the broken stone steps, just like when they used to cool off in the courtyard as children. He didn't rush to probe the details of those years, simply listening quietly. Chen Nian spoke in fragments—after being taken by the Holy Sect, she nearly died in a sacrificial ritual, until that "person who shouldn't exist" appeared.

choices.description: "Who saved you? What is this Tianji Pavilion branch?" Get the most critical information first.
choices.risk_hint: May Destroy the Rare Warm Atmosphere

text.content: Chen Ji fell silent for a moment before finally asking the question. Chen Nian froze, then smiled bitterly: "You're still the same, brother. But it's fine, I understand—you have too many people to protect, so you must first know where the danger lies." Her gaze deepened. "The one who saved me... was no ordinary person. He came from the Tianji Pavilion."

dialogue.content: "Tianji Pavilion?" Mo Xiansheng's voice suddenly exploded from the Tianji Record, shock barely concealed. "Impossible! The Tianji Pavilion ceased to exist three thousand years ago... Are you certain this was the name?" Chen Ji's expression remained unchanged, but internally, waves were churning—if something could unsettle this old fox, the Tianji Pavilion was by no means an ordinary force.

choices.description: "You mentioned being able to see threads of fate... what does that mean?" Understand her ability first before making judgments.
choices.visible_reward: Understand the Nature of Chen Nian's Ability

text.content: Chen Nian wiped away the tears at the corners of her eyes, her expression gradually becoming grave. "That is... an ability I obtained after being rescued." She raised her hand and gestured in the void. "I can see the threads on everyone. Those threads connect to their destinies—love and hate, joy and sorrow, life and death, all tangled upon that single thread."

She suddenly leaned close to Chen Ji, her gaze falling upon a certain part of his body, her complexion abruptly changing. "Brother, on you..." Chen Ji's heart tightened. "What about me?" Chen Nian's voice began to tremble. "You are being watched by two... two different eyes. One in the heavens, and another... in a deeper place."

dialogue.content: Chen Nian took a deep breath, as if organizing her words. "Brother, there are two threads on you. One is golden, very bright and thick—that should be... the power of the Tianji Record. It's connected to the Heavenly Dao's Eye, and I can see the end of that thread—it's a massive vortex." Her voice grew lower. "But the other one... is black. Much thinner, yet much deeper. It spreads from the soles of your feet, extending all the way to... a place I cannot see."

"Black thread..." Mo Xiansheng's voice fell uncharacteristically silent for several breaths before speaking again, carrying a trace of gravity. "This old man has lived for so many years and only seen that color on one person. That is... an existence older than the Heavenly Dao." He paused. "Chen Ji, your chess game may have been watched from the very beginning. Not by the Heavenly Dao, but by something else."

text.content: Chen Ji did not speak. His expression remained calm, terrifyingly so. His fingers tapped lightly on his knee—once, twice, thrice—this was his habit when thinking. Mo Xiansheng's voice, the gaze of the Heavenly Dao's Eye, and Chen Nian's mention of "the eye in the deeper place"... these fragments rapidly combined in his mind, piecing together a possibility that sent a chill down his spine.

dialogue.content: Chen Nian suddenly grabbed his wrist, her grip shockingly strong. Her eyes were fixed on a certain point in the void, her pupils constricting sharply. "Brother! It... it's looking at you! That eye, it knows I can see it—" Her voice cut off abruptly, her body freezing as if she had witnessed something utterly terrifying.

choice.prompt: Faced with this sudden abnormal change, how should Chen Ji respond?

choices.description: "Don't be afraid, brother is here." Pull her behind me, positioning myself between her and "that eye".
choices.visible_reward: Protecting my sister's safety and trust
choices.risk_hint: Not knowing the opponent's background, I might suffer a loss

text.content: Chen Ji's action was faster than his thought. He pulled Chen Nian behind him in one swift motion, positioning himself in front of her. In that instant, he felt an invisible pressure pouring down from above, as if something was scrutinizing him—examining the Tianji Record within him, his machinations over the years, even his current choice.

choices.description: Proactively channel the power of the Tianji Record to see the true form of that "eye".
choices.risk_hint: Heavenly Fate might deplete rapidly, and the opponent will notice
choices.process_label: resist mysterious gaze with tianji power

text.content: A sharp light flashed in Chen Ji's eyes, the Tianji Record Fragment trembling violently within his consciousness. He endured the needle-like pain piercing his mind, struggling to grasp the source of that gaze. Yet in that moment, he witnessed—within the boundless darkness, an eye was slowly opening. Within that pupil, the trajectories of heaven and earth were reflected, while he himself was merely an insignificant point.

choices.description: This place is unsuitable for lingering; let's take Chen Nian and leave first.
choices.risk_hint: Potentially miss critical information, and the opponent might track us

text.content: "Go!" Chen Ji shouted, grabbing Chen Nian's hand and rushing outside. His intuition was screaming in alarm—this place could no longer be stayed in. Yet the instant they burst through the temple door, Chen Nian grabbed him violently. "Brother! It... it smiled." Her voice trembled. "That eye smiled. It said... 'Finally found you.'"

Outside the broken temple, the morning mist had somehow dissipated. The sunlight fell upon his body, yet it could not dispel the coldness in Chen Ji's heart. Mo Xiansheng's voice rang out slowly, carrying an unprecedented gravity: 'Chen Ji, your sister is right. This chess game is far larger than you and I imagined. The Heavenly Secrets Eye is merely a piece on the chessboard... and that thing, is the true Chess Player.'

Chen Ji stood outside the broken temple, turning back to glance at the shattered Buddha's head. Ten years of layout, he thought he was the one playing the game. But now it seemed he was merely the most crucial piece on the chessboard—a piece calculated from the very beginning. His fists tightened gently, knuckles whitening. Chen Nian stood beside him, softly taking his hand: 'Brother, whatever comes, I'll face it with you.'

Chen Ji did not answer. He merely gently held his sister's hand back, those eyes that could calculate everything gazed at a certain spot in the sky, his expression dark and indecipherable. After a moment, he spoke in a low voice, his tone so calm that no emotion could be discerned: 'I've noted it down.' These three words, spoken from his mouth, carried more weight than any oath.

Chen Nian pointed into the Void, where those invisible eyes were watching—it was more terrifying than the Heavenly Secrets Eye, because it was the Chess Player weaving this ten-thousand-year chess game. 'Brother, those eyes... are more terrifying than the Heavenly Secrets Eye.' Her voice was soft, yet every word was clear, 'It is weaving a chess game spanning ten thousand years. And we, perhaps from the moment we were born, have already been placed on the board.' The morning wind suddenly rose, stirring the loose hair by her temples, and also scattering the last trace of warmth from the broken temple.
